title.narrative: IPE - Integrated Protection and Education Initiative for community resilience in Qudsiya, Rural Damascus.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project is designed to address the critical needs of vulnerable populations in Qudsiya affected by conflict, displacement, and socio-economic crises. By focusing on two strategic priorities—delivering life-saving humanitarian aid and building long-term resilience—the project aims to support and strengthen the delivery of essential services to those most in need under the sectors of Protection and Education, while strengthening community-based protection mechanisms. In line with SHF allocation, the intervention will apply a multi-sector and integrated approach addressing multiple needs of beneficiaries, providing them with different services. ltbrgt ltbrgtUnder the Protection sector, the project will implement a range of activities, including parenting skills sessions, psychosocial support (PSS) for children, and awareness campaigns on gender and menstrual hygiene. Additionally, dignity kits will be distributed to women and girls, and volunteers will receive training on psychosocial approach. These Protection activities will be carried out in collaboration with SARC (Syrian Arab Red Crescent) through SARC mobile units, which serves a large number of beneficiaries, to maximize impact and outreach. ltbrgt ltbrgtUnder the Education sector the action focuses on education and resilience-building for communities affected by ongoing crises. In partnership with the Ministry of Education (MoE), the project will offer a comprehensive educational support package that includes catch-up and remedial classes to address learning gaps, BTL campaigns to boost community engagement in education, and the provision of essential furniture and equipment to enhance school environments. The project will also assist students during national exams and carry out light renovations at Qudsaya Fourth Mixed Primary School, with a focus on improving safety, upgrading WASH facilities, increasing energy independence, and enhancing the school's aesthetics to foster a dignitous learning environment. ltbrgtIn addition, Second Qudsaya School will benefit from the installation of a solar power system to support energy sustainability. ltbrgtTeachers will be trained in active learning techniques and Pyschosocial Approach (PSA), enhancing the quality of education and supporting the mental and emotional well-being of students. ltbrgt ltbrgtBeneficiaries identified as facing protection risks in either sector will be referred to SARC case managers through a secure referral pathway. ltbrgtIndeed, targeting the same area for both Education and Protection activities allows for a holistic approach, where beneficiaries overlap, enhancing their overall well-being. This comprehensive support system addresses multiple vulnerabilities simultaneously, reducing risks and building community resilience. Additionally, capacity building for teachers and SARC staff ensures the project's sustainability, empowering local actors to continue delivering high-quality services post-project. ltbrgtlt/pgt
